title: VideoSource
description: One footage source in the archive: an uploaded recording, a configured live camera, or the replay fixture that drives the live path in demos. Every downstream record names the source and clock it came from, so a timestamp is never ambiguous.

source_id.description: Stable identifier for this footage source. Referenced by every observation, event, window and evidence record.

camera_id.description: Physical camera or recording position. Two sources may share a camera_id (e.g. a recording and its live feed) and are then treated as the same viewpoint for search.

kind.description: recorded_upload = a file uploaded by a human. live_feed = a configured RTSP/HTTP camera. replay = a sample file pushed through the live code path for demos, which must behave identically to live_feed everywhere downstream.

clock.description: Which clock produced the timestamps for this source. source_clock = timestamps came from the camera or container metadata and are trusted as absolute. ingestion_clock = timestamps were stamped when the feed was read, so they are absolute but late by the network and buffer delay. media_relative_only = no wall-clock anchor exists; only offsets from the start of the file are meaningful.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used to render and resolve local times for this source, e.g. Asia/Riyadh. Required so 'yesterday' and 'around 4 PM' resolve to the same instants the user means.

venue_id.description: Location the source belongs to. The chat scopes searches by venue before ranking.

location_label.description: Human description of what this camera covers, e.g. 'Classroom 3 doorway'. Used in answers; never invented — null when unknown.

recording_started_at.description: Absolute UTC instant corresponding to media offset 0. Required for calendar questions ('yesterday morning') on recorded_upload sources; null when the file has no reliable anchor. Never guessed from file modification time.

recording_ended_at.description: Absolute UTC instant of the last frame, or null when unknown or the source is still live.

media_path.description: Path or URI to the media, relative to the configured media root. Never a public URL for private footage.

duration_seconds.description: Media duration when known. Null for a live feed.

fps_nominal.description: Nominal frame rate from the container. Sampling decisions use this, not an assumed 30fps.

resolution.description: Nominal frame size, used when scoring whether a model can see a jacket at all.

audio_present.description: Audio is off by default for this project. Set true only for expressly approved clips, and note it in access notes.

access.description: Who may see this footage and its derived evidence. Enforced when serving clips and when returning search results.

visibility.description: public_demo = staged or expressly approved clip, safe to serve to judges. approved_private = real footage with a named approval on file; never served without an authorisation check. internal_only = working material, never served.

approved_by.description: Who approved use of this footage. Null for public_demo fixtures and for internal_only material.

expires_at.description: When the footage must stop being retained and served. Null means no scheduled expiry.

notes.description: Free text: how to obtain the file, known occlusion, mounting quirks. Never a secret, stream credential or token.
